details:
Project Title: After the Mission: The Stories of Machines That Stayed Behind

Our project is an educational digital magazine that explores the stories of spacecraft, rovers, landers, and other machines that remain in space or on other worlds after their missions end.

The magazine explains why these machines were sent into space, what they achieved, why their missions ended, and what happened to them afterward. It features missions such as Apollo, Viking, Spirit, Opportunity, Curiosity, Perseverance, Ingenuity, Dawn, and Kepler.

The project is presented as an interactive digital flipbook, making space exploration information easy and interesting to read. It includes mission stories, comparisons, timelines, illustrations, and educational content to help readers understand the history and lasting impact of space exploration.

The main benefit of this project is to make space science more accessible and engaging, especially for students and young learners. It encourages curiosity about astronomy, engineering, robotics, and future space missions.

Our goal is to remind people that a space mission's story does not end when communication stops or the mission is over. The machines left behind remain part of humanity's journey into space.

The project is published online using Heyzine as a digital flipbook.
